newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-BAGGIO SAYS "THANKS BUT NOT YET" TO NAPOLI.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-BAGGIO SAYS "THANKS BUT NOT YET" TO NAPOLI.

text.p: Striker Roberto Baggio said on Saturday that he planned to stay at Milan for the rest of the season despite the frustrations of having to spend most of it so far on the substitutes' bench.

The 29-year-old "Divine Ponytail" told Corriere dello Sport newspaper that he had been flattered by an open invitation from Napoli general director Ottavio Bianchi to move there but had no plans for the moment to leave the struggling Italian champions.
"Obviously I'm very pleased to hear that somebody still believes in me given that I've gone out of fashion for a lot of people, Baggio said.

"The offer from Napoli, if it comes, is something I can think about calmly a bit down the road. But apart from the enormous pleasure it gives me, what I'm thinking about now is Milan and nothing else."

Baggio, who is reported to have a frosty relationship with new coach Arrigo Sacchi, has played just 632 minutes of serie A soccer this season and is expected to be on the bench again when Milan play Vicenza on Sunday.

He said he believed the team, out of European and domestic cup competition after a dismal start to the season, could still win the league and made clear his sights were also set on a return to Italian side.

Baggio missed in a penalty shoot-out Italy lost to Brazil in the World Cup final in Los Angeles in 1994, when Sacchi was coach, and has not played for his country since he came on as a substitute in a 1-0 win against Slovenia in September 1995.
"My aim is to play for Italy again and take part in the World Cup finals," Baggio said.
"But to get back in the national side I have to play. That is my biggest problem at the moment," he said.
